summary: A brick tower on a steel pier, built 1907-1910 on a bare reef off Isle Royale; its keepers sheltered the passengers of the wrecked steamer George M. Cox in 1933.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree and the story says so: first light 22 Oct 1908 (Pepper, LighthouseFriends) vs 11 Oct (NPS); start of construction 1907 (LighthouseFriends, NPS) vs 1908 (Pepper); total cost $138,328.50 vs $125,000; Keller as captain (NPS) vs major (Pepper); lens range 19 miles (1912 description via LighthouseFriends) vs 29 (NPS); crew served to 1977 (NPS) vs automation 1978 (USLHS, ROALPS); Cox wreck date 27 May (LighthouseFriends, a 28 May newspaper saying Saturday evening) vs 28 May (Pepper), and persons: 127 aboard, 116 landed (Bulletin) vs 125 (Pepper); Pepper's third assistant 'Marrow' vs Bulletin/archive Heinsberg. The Bulletin OCR reads the Cox date as 'May 2:l'. LighthouseFriends dates the keepers' walk-out to Dec 1926; the 1918-1923 Bulletin index has a Marigold pick-up entry for the station (p. 113) which cannot be the 1926 event if that date is right; no primary text on the 1926 event was found. Muessel (interview) calls an assistant 'Ed Hinesburg'/'Hubert Veislaw' predecessor; the roster has Heinsberg and Beyschlag; not linked in the story. Muessel's USLHS record gives 1918-2016. Roster years for head keepers overlap (Metivier to at least 1926, Mueller from 1925). Bulletin 1936 page is the 1936_0 file. NRHP nomination PDF is not digitised; listing date taken from NPGallery metadata. USCG Historian page was not retrievable from the archive. Newspapers read: Bismarck Tribune (AP-style story) and Brownsville Herald pages; I did not read the Evening Star. Agency/ownership of the tower is not stated in the sources read, so the story gives none. 1912 description quoted by LighthouseFriends, not read in the original. Fact-check: Pepper spells the first head keeper 'Ervine' once and 'Irvine' once; story and roster use Irvine. Muessel's 24-foot boat crossing was for liberty, not supplies (corrected). Crawford destination differs (Pepper Two Harbors, LighthouseFriends Houghton). Printed page of the 1900 report not verified, so cited by scan page. No OCR-table matching by column position.
